summary.text: Lance Gooden is the Republican U.S. Representative for Texas's 5th Congressional District and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.
A Terrell resident who worked in the insurance industry, he served three terms in the Texas House before his 2018 election to Congress, where he sits on the Judiciary and Armed Services committees.

paragraphs.text: Gooden was born in Nashville, Tennessee, in 1982; according to Wikipedia he was raised in Terrell, Texas, in Kaufman County. He earned a bachelor's degree in finance and government from the University of Texas in 2004.
He worked as an insurance broker and risk-management consultant, and his official biography says he spent 10 years in the insurance industry.

Gooden served in the Texas House of Representatives (District 4, covering parts of Henderson and Kaufman counties) from 2011 to 2015 and from 2017 to 2019, three terms in all; Wikipedia reports he lost the 2014 Republican primary before returning to the seat in 2016.

He was first elected to Congress in 2018 and took office January 3, 2019, succeeding Jeb Hensarling. His district stretches from Dallas County to Henderson, Kaufman, Van Zandt, Wood and Upshur counties.

In the 119th Congress he serves on the House Judiciary Committee and the House Armed Services Committee. According to his official biography, he lives in Terrell with his wife, Alexa, and their two children.
Gooden won the November 3, 2026 general election with 51.5% of the vote to Chelsey Hockett's 48.5%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
